name: vap-audit-pod-procA
why: Procedure A: a user creates a pod with a disallowed image under an Audit-mode VAP binding -- the server admits it and writes the validation_failure event annotation (the chokepoint, audit branch)
source: recorded on a local kube-apiserver v1.36.4 lab (etcd + kube-apiserver + kube-controller-manager) running atomics/T1204.003/src/emulate.sh a; shape matches apiserver .../admission/plugin/policy/validating/dispatcher.go @ v1.36.4 (publishValidationFailureAnnotation / denied-request message). The annotation value is byte-for-byte the recorded one.

annotations.validation.policy.admission.k8s.io/valid: [{"message":"image not allowed: every container image must be digest-pinned (contain @sha256:)","policy":"trr9034-image-provenance","binding":"trr9034-image-provenance-audit","expressionIndex":0,"validationActions":["Audit"]}]

name: vap-deny-pod-procB
why: Procedure B: a user creates a pod with a disallowed image under a Deny-mode VAP binding -- the server refuses it (422 Invalid) with the denied-request message (the chokepoint, deny branch)
source: recorded on the local kube-apiserver v1.36.4 lab (atomics/T1204.003/src/emulate.sh b); shape matches apiserver .../admission/plugin/policy/validating/dispatcher.go @ v1.36.4 (publishValidationFailureAnnotation / denied-request message). The responseStatus is byte-for-byte the recorded refusal (code 422, reason Invalid).

responseStatus.message: pods "trr9034-deny-web" is forbidden: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 'trr9034-image-provenance' with binding 'trr9034-image-provenance-deny' denied request: image not allowed: every container image must be digest-pinned (contain @sha256:)

name: vap-audit-controller-pod-procC
why: Procedure C: a Deployment whose pod template has a disallowed image -- the controller's own pods create (by generateName, so objectRef carries no name) bears the annotation. The rule must NOT filter controller identities, or the indirect path is missed.
source: shape recorded on the local kube-apiserver v1.36.4 lab (atomics/T1204.003/src/emulate.sh c): a controller pods create with no objectRef.name and the annotation, admitted 201. The lab's controller authenticates as system:kube-controller-manager (static token); a per-SA-token cluster (kind) records system:serviceaccount:kube-system:replicaset-controller, shown here. The rule reads neither identity.

annotations.validation.policy.admission.k8s.io/valid: [{"message":"image not allowed: every container image must be digest-pinned (contain @sha256:)","policy":"trr9034-image-provenance","binding":"trr9034-image-provenance-audit","expressionIndex":0,"validationActions":["Audit"]}]

name: allowed-image-pod
why: the hard benign baseline: the same pod create with an allowlisted, digest-pinned image. The VAP admits it and writes NO annotation, so the audit marker is the single flip -- restore it and the rule fires.
source: synthetic (apiserver .../admission/plugin/policy/validating/dispatcher.go @ v1.36.4 (publishValidationFailureAnnotation / denied-request message)); atomics/T1204.003/src/emulate.sh allow.

name: rbac-forbidden-pod
why: a pod create REFUSED by RBAC, not by a VAP: responseStatus is a Forbidden, but its message is not the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy denied-request message, so the deny clause must be load-bearing (a plain 403 must not fire).
source: synthetic (apimachinery .../api/errors NewForbidden @ v1.36.4: '<resource> is forbidden: User ... cannot create ...').

responseStatus.message: pods is forbidden: User "trr9034-attacker" cannot create resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "trr9034"

name: vap-verdict-on-configmap
why: a VAP label/quota policy verdict on a ConfigMap (a non-workload resource) carries the same annotation; the rule is scoped to workloads (where an image lives), so resource is the single flip. A non-image VAP verdict is not a malicious-image event.
source: synthetic (apiserver .../admission/plugin/policy/validating/dispatcher.go @ v1.36.4 (publishValidationFailureAnnotation / denied-request message)); a site label-policy VAP bound to configmaps.

name: client-set-object-annotation
why: an actor sets an OBJECT annotation of the same key in the pod it creates; it lands in requestObject.metadata.annotations, NOT in the event-level annotations the server controls, so it must not fire (provenance confounder).
source: synthetic: a client cannot set an event-level audit annotation (apiserver audit context.go AddAuditAnnotation is server-only); an object annotation of the same name is requestObject.metadata.annotations.

name: psa-audit-violation
why: Pod Security Admission writes a different built-in event annotation (pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit-violations) on the same pod create; it is a different key and field, so the VAP rule must not fire on it.
source: synthetic: PodSecurity admission plugin audit annotation (apiserver .../admission/plugin/policy ... PodSecurity; distinct key).

name: ordinary-deployment-create
why: an ordinary Deployment create on a cluster with no Audit/Deny VAP bound to it: no verdict annotation, no denied-request message, admitted. Must not fire.
source: synthetic: a routine apps/v1 Deployment create.
